goal: Let a recruiter and Para AI jointly manage one candidate across every opportunity they're active in, with Para AI organizing context and handling bounded coordination while the recruiter retains control of relationship-sensitive decisions.
user_segments: Para AI (system actor with bounded autonomy)
success_metrics: Less recruiter time spent coordinating one candidate across roles
Fewer opportunities go stale from missed follow-up
Recruiters keep auto-execution on, not off
Recruiters act on Para AI's recommendations more often than not
Zero relationship-sensitive actions sent without recruiter approval
constraints: Recruiter must remain the decision-maker on relationship-sensitive actions
Para AI actions must be traceable to a specific context source
Take-home exercise scope, no existing internal Paraform spec to reconcile against
Candidate profiles are owned per recruiter, not shared platform-wide — this feature does not reconcile or dedupe across recruiters
assumptions: Resume and LinkedIn data default to Visible to Para AI; notes and call recordings default to Private
Exactly one recruiter owns a given candidate profile at a time, by platform architecture rather than a v1 scoping choice
Company-to-opportunity mapping is reliable enough to auto-detect same-company double submission
Auto-executed actions are limited to reversible, logistical communications
Para AI can surface opportunity matches beyond the recruiter's own submissions; such matches require recruiter confirmation before becoming an active track
gaps: Bulk-approve interaction is underspecified and risks becoming a rubber stamp
"Undo" on auto-executed actions is not literally possible for already-sent communications
No cross-recruiter identity resolution or deduplication — same real person could be independently submitted to the same role by two recruiters
Whether Para AI's platform-wide matching reach always routes through the same recruiter-confirmation gate as a recruiter-initiated submission is unconfirmed
No notification mechanism defined for a recruiter's cross-candidate approval backlog now that there is no per-candidate Action Queue to check
Whether a flat 60-90 day staleness threshold is right for all volatile context or should vary by fact type
edge_cases: Candidate declines one opportunity while active in others
Source excluded from matching after Para AI already used it in a recommendation
Para AI proposes double submission to the same hiring company
Approval-required action left unactioned past the timeout window
Call recording fails to transcribe or produces low-confidence output
Candidate withdraws from the process entirely
Same real-world candidate independently owned by another recruiter — out of scope to detect or reconcile
Para AI surfaces a new opportunity match the recruiter did not initiate — requires recruiter confirmation before becoming active, shown in a distinct Proposed section
Volatile context item ages past staleness threshold — flagged for reconfirmation, matching weight discounted
Durable context item ages — never flagged as stale

critical_questions.question: Should notes/calls default to Visible-to-Para-AI to maximize context, or Private to maximize trust and control?
Is there any candidate-facing view, or is the candidate purely the subject and never a user of this system?
Is company-to-opportunity mapping reliable enough today to auto-block same-company double submission?
Is automatic call-recording sync from a connected tool assumed to exist, or is manual upload the only real v1 path?
Can Para AI surface a match to an opportunity the recruiter hasn't chosen, and does entering it always require recruiter confirmation the same way a recruiter-initiated submission does?
Does Paraform perform any identity resolution across independently-owned recruiter profiles for the same real person, to catch duplicate submissions to the same role?

design_risks: Bulk approval without forced per-item review turns the approval gate into a formality
Over-cautious visibility defaults starve Para AI of context and defeat the feature's stated purpose
Labeling a sent-and-undeliverable-to-retract email as 'undo' sets a false expectation and breaks trust when discovered
If the auto-executed vs. approval-required distinction isn't visible everywhere an action appears, recruiters are surprised by actions they didn't know had already gone out

Cross-recruiter duplicate submission of the same candidate to the same role is not solvable within one recruiter's Opportunities view and should be surfaced as a known limitation, not implied as handled
Para AI's matching reach could outpace recruiter awareness if a surfaced match isn't reliably gated behind recruiter confirmation before anything moves forward
A staleness indicator not backed by real recency-weighting in the matching logic would mislead recruiters the same way a false 'undo' does
teaching_notes: The brief's 'Passive Placements' reference implies Para AI already has a submission-recommendation capability; frame this feature as extending that muscle across concurrent opportunities, not inventing new AI capability
Approval-required items expand inline on their opportunity row (same fast approve/edit/reject interaction as a triage inbox) rather than living behind a separate Action Queue destination
Auto-executed vs. Recruiter-approval-required is the single most important piece of information architecture and must be a persistent, legible signal everywhere an action or its status appears
Opportunities is the default landing view (task-oriented); Profile & Context is secondary and on-demand (data-oriented) — default design decisions toward keeping recruiters on Opportunities
